_note: Editorial Caspian-basin oil movements. Iran sends ~none of its OWN crude north across the (landlocked) Caspian — its export terminals are all on the Gulf (Kharg). Iran's actual Caspian oil activity is the NEKA SWAP: Russian/Kazakh/Turkmen crude is tankered IN to Neka for Iran's northern refineries, and Iran delivers an EQUIVALENT volume of its own crude OUT at the Gulf. So 'Iranian oil through the Caspian' = actual swap throughput, which is small and intermittent (far below the ~370k bpd Neka terminal capacity). All bpd are dated editorial estimates with sources; rounded, not precise telemetry. Edit freely.
